# Local image attachments

[English](attachments.md) | [日本語](../../../ja/api/v1/attachments.md) | [Français](../../../fr/api/v1/attachments.md) | [中文](../../../api/v1/attachments.md)

<!-- Generated by npm run docs:localize; edit docs/i18n/translations.json. -->

All attachment routes use local-owner authentication and the existing data domain. Only static PNG/JPEG are accepted after byte-based format validation and full decoding; animation, MPO, trailing bytes and other formats are rejected. No conversion, resizing or EXIF removal occurs: original metadata, possibly including location, is sent with the image to the selected provider.

## Import and messages

First POST `/api/v1/attachments/import`, freezing request_id, absolute source_path, expected_sha256, decimal-string expected_bytes and display name. Ancestor directories may be symlinks, but the final component must be a regular file, not a symlink. Core never deletes the source file.

202 means only that the reservation is durable. Poll GET `/api/v1/requests/{id}`; delete a client temporary file only after COMPLETED and an attachment_id in result. The separate import queue moves directly from QUEUED to COMPLETED or FAILED, bypassing generic RUNNING/UNKNOWN. Uncertain IO retains QUEUED and quota and may report ATTACHMENT_IMPORT_RETRY_REQUIRED; restore IO and restart to recover with the same ID and complete body.

Then POST `/api/v1/messages` with a different request_id, text and ordered attachment_ids. Image-only text="" is allowed; whitespace-only text and duplicate attachment IDs are rejected. Reusing a ready ID explicitly resends its image. Changing any submitted field under the same ID conflicts. Completed imports keep their fixed CAS originals after source deletion or replacement.

GET `/api/v1/attachments/{id}`, timeline and message content expose lightweight metadata only. Explicit GET `/api/v1/attachments/{id}/content` returns verified original binary with length, ETag, no-store and nosniff; ranges are unsupported. Runtime corruption returns 410 ATTACHMENT_UNAVAILABLE. Missing or truncated durable references fail Store.open on restart.

## Deployment and budgets

The defaults below can be lowered using environment variables SECRETARY_ATTACHMENT_ plus the uppercase field name, but never exceeded. Lower limits do not delete old content; pending imports retain admission-time validation ceilings. Full quota rejects new imports, not existing attachment sends. New identities for identical content are charged separately; failed identities remain counted, and byte reservations remain when CAS may exist. There is no automatic cleanup, age expiry or unbound deletion.

| Field | Default |
| --- | ---: |
| `file_bytes` | 5242880 |
| `side` | 4096 |
| `pixels` | 4194304 |
| `message_count` | 4 |
| `message_bytes` | 10485760 |
| `reserved_bytes` | 1073741824 |
| `import_count` | 10000 |
| `wire_bytes` | 25165824 |

SECRETARY_VISION_BUDGET_PROFILES is a JSON array, default []. Each entry must exactly match provider, api, model and normalized baseUrl, with version=1, positive-integer tokens_per_image, max_side, max_pixels and a nonempty source rationale. Deployment owners select real limits from provider documentation; 8192 is an offline fixture bound only, never a universal default. Without a match capabilities.attachments.allowed=false and sending returns ATTACHMENT_BUDGET_UNCONFIGURED; text-only models return ATTACHMENT_MODEL_UNSUPPORTED.

The profile constrains admission, dispatch, final adapter payload and frozen request replay. Final image order, MIME and digests must match the input. Token estimation removes base64 in a copy and adds the per-image ceiling; wire limits are checked separately. Text-only identities and policy_id remain unchanged. Aggregate evidence stores versioned CAS references and verifies the original JSON digest during exact hydration; per-message CAS retains full content.

K=0: images remain complete throughout their handling loop, tool iterations and frozen replay. New loops after HANDLED retain authenticated metadata explicitly stating that this request has no pixels. Adjacent follow-ups do not resend images automatically; the owner must explicitly reuse a ready ID. Summaries read typed text and uninspected metadata; commitment extraction reads original typed text only. An image source cannot become a MASTER fact solely through input.accepted.

## Withdrawal and recovery

POST `/api/v1/inputs/{id}/withdraw` uses a new request_id and expected_revision to withdraw the entire attachment input, including text. Host and maintenance must be idle; CLAIMED also requires a blocked exclusive loop, no assistant output, no IN_FLIGHT/RESPONSE_SAVED and no pending or executed tool effects. Otherwise return 409 WITHDRAWAL_UNSAFE. Safe withdrawal commits Context/Input/Session/events/ApiCommand in one frame; the notice enters only one subsequent loop, while history remains marked withdrawn.

Withdrawn inputs are excluded from new summaries, commitments, search hits and World evidence. Old candidates are rechecked before publication; lagging search indexes also apply current withdrawal filtering. Audit originals remain. Stale IN_FLIGHT from a dead process cannot be withdrawn: restore the previously supported deployment and use existing recovery. #80 recovery policy is unchanged.

## Dependencies and validation boundaries

sharp is pinned to 0.35.5 (Apache-2.0); the lockfile includes Linux/macOS native optional dependencies. libvips and component licenses are in the installed LICENSE/README files; preserve their notices when distributing. Portable packaging is outside this issue. Core contracts use installed adapters against local HTTP fixtures. Real provider vision is NOT_TESTED; #84 prepares the profile and synthetic smoke. New TUI consumption and human terminal experience remain unaccepted.
